name: Zabad
overview: Zabad is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra as a descendant of Hashum. His distinct identification comes from the fact that he was among those who had married a foreign wife, a matter addressed in the post-exilic community's efforts to maintain covenantal purity. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Zabad means 'he bestows' in the original Hebrew. This proper name, while not indicated as given directly by God, reflects a common theophoric or meaningful naming practice in the Old Testament, though no specific title or further significance is attached to it in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Zabad was a descendant of Hashum, establishing a genealogical link important for identifying individuals in the post-exilic community. Beyond this, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Zabad's mention in Ezra 10:33 highlights his role within the community's struggle to uphold the covenant by addressing intermarriage with foreign wives. His inclusion underscores the collective responsibility and challenges faced by the returned exiles in reestablishing faithfulness to God's commands. Though a minor figure, Zabad represents the broader narrative of restoration and purity in Israel's history after the Babylonian exile.
